title: OCCURS ... ASCENDING KEY IS — SEARCH ALL is binary search; table MUST be pre-sorted
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PRICE-LOOKUP.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-PRICES.
           05  WS-PRICE-ROW OCCURS 100 TIMES
                            ASCENDING KEY IS WS-SKU
                            INDEXED BY WS-IX.
               10  WS-SKU     PIC X(10).
               10  WS-AMOUNT  PIC 9(7)V99.
      *> SEARCH ALL does a binary search and REQUIRES the table to
      *> be sorted on WS-SKU. If the load step skipped the sort,
      *> SEARCH ALL silently returns 'not found' for valid keys.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       LOOKUP-PRICE.
           SEARCH ALL WS-PRICE-ROW
              AT END DISPLAY "not found"
              WHEN WS-SKU(WS-IX) = "AAA-001"
                 DISPLAY WS-AMOUNT(WS-IX).
notes: SEARCH ALL is one of the trickiest COBOL constructs — fast binary search if the precondition is met, silent failure if not. The spec must capture: (a) the binary-search semantic, (b) the sorted-precondition invariant, and (c) where the sort happens (often a separate program that ran before this one).
